title: Mean Corpuscular Hemoglobin Concentration (MCHC)

references.label: Standard clinical hematology laboratory textbooks/manuals (e.g. Henry's Clinical Diagnosis and Management)

explanation: MCHC expresses the average concentration of hemoglobin within a given volume of packed red cells (unlike MCH, which is a mass per cell). A low MCHC (hypochromia) suggests red cells are relatively hemoglobin-poor for their size, classically associated with iron-deficiency-pattern anemias, while a normal or elevated MCHC pattern points elsewhere in the differential — again, only in combination with MCV, MCH, and clinical findings, never from MCHC alone.

workedExample.scenario: A hemoglobin of 15 g/dL and a hematocrit of 45%.

commonMistakes: Confusing MCHC (a concentration, independent of cell count) with MCH (a mass per cell) — the two answer different questions and are not interchangeable.
